title: SPARK CSEC Physics - Paper 01 Practice Paper 12
subject: Physics
syllabus: CXC 22/G/SYLL 13, for examinations from May and June 2015
instructions: This test consists of 60 items. You will have 1 hour and 15 minutes to answer them.
Each item has four suggested answers lettered A, B, C and D. Choose the best answer.
If you cannot answer an item, move on and return to it later.
Figures are not necessarily drawn to scale.
You may use a silent, non-programmable calculator.

items.objective_statement: draw a line of ‘best fit’ for a set of plotted values
items.stem: A best-fit line is preferred to a line joining successive plotted points because it

misconception.label: Being easier to draw is not a reason for preferring it.

options.text: averages out the uncertainty in the individual readings

misconception.label: Only a relationship of direct proportion passes through the origin.

options.text: is always steeper than the joined line

misconception.label: The gradient of the best fit line is whatever the readings give; it is not systematically steeper.

steps: Every reading carries a small error, so no single point is exactly right.
Joining the points repeats those errors in the shape of the line.
A single line drawn with the points balanced above and below it averages the errors out, so its gradient is the best estimate available.

items.stem: Which observation provided evidence against the caloric theory?

options.text: A hot drink cools when left standing

misconception.label: Caloric flowing out of the drink into the air explains this.

options.text: A metal spoon in hot soup becomes hot

misconception.label: Caloric flowing along the spoon explains this.

options.text: Rubbing two dry sticks together produces heat without limit
